chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Claude's artistic control, her name change and early publicity
summary: Claude's role was artistic, he picked the name Sullivan, and she tells how Archer Winston's article came about.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

rather active involvement.
Yes he did. But Claude was strictly in an artistic sense. Claude had no business.
Okay, but could I just ask this though? He was associated in some way with your name change from Marietta Williams to Maxine Sullivan.

When I came to New York I had been using the name Maxine Williams at the B.H.L. Club. But I think I mentioned previously that, well there was a singer making recordings and was on the air by the name of Midge Williams and I guess he supposed there would be some sort of a conflict, and it was his idea to change the name to Sullivan.
You don't know where he got the name from?

I don't know. He may have done this because he had a definite idea of what he wanted me to do, performance wise. The mere selection of 'Loch Loman', 'Annie Laurie', and the traditional folk songs, to identify me or disassociate me from the average singer.
Right.
And it was a novel idea. I
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

don't know whether the suggestion of the name Sullivan had anything to do with his particular attitude or approach. I do know that in the beginning when I was at the Onyx Club he was very adament about photographs being taken of me as opposed - he didn't want anybody to realize at the time that I was black.

Actually, when you were talking with Art Vincent in New York I didn't quite hear exactly what you were saying, but you were saying something about him being opposed to you having your photograph taken for publicity purposes?

Yeah, well I didn't know anything about publicity at that time, but you know, the mere fact that I had swung luck and got all this notoriety, there were alot of people coming in, reporters I suppose and I didn't even realize it to take pictures. And as I said before he got pretty adament about that. And he didn't particularly want it known that I was a black singer. Where in fact, I suppose, I must have been at the Onyx, and after the exposure on the air and also at Loew's State Theatre with the band that appeared on the Saturday Night Swing Club, there was no denying at this

particular point, and this is when Archer Winston came out with this article about Modern Svengali Discovers..... ."
As you suggested before there's a glimmer of truth in that - there's a hint of accuracy, that he was controlling - - I don't mean in a sinister way.
Yeah, this is true.
To your artistic destiny.

Well I suppose he felt he had something here, had a little gem here and he didn't want anybody to cut in. Of course, he would know more about that than I would. I didn't realize there would be anything like somebody else wanting to take credit, you know, for whatever had been done. I suppose it's just like even today, if you have a property you want to hold on to it, and as I said before, Claude not being of the business nature, he probably felt that any minute I was going to lose this thing which eventually he did, because the whole situation was bigger than Claude could handle. And later on I was approached by an attorney, you know, who wanted to know the situation.
